fix_commit_message:
BIO_send/recvmmsg(): Pass msgs_processed to the return callback

This avoids crash if a legacy BIO callback is set and
BIO_sendmmsg() or BIO_recvmmsg() is used.

Reported by Stanislav Fort (Aisle Research)

Reviewed-by: Matt Caswell <matt@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Norbert Pocs <norbertp@openssl.org>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/29395)
agent_reasoning: The introducing commit ("Make s_client -quic -debug work") changed the `inret` argument passed to bio_call_callback() for the BIO_CB_SENDMMSG/BIO_CB_RECVMMSG return callbacks from a hard-coded 0 to the actual return value `ret`. This reactivated a code path inside bio_call_callback() that dereferences the `processed` out-parameter whenever `inret > 0` for legacy callbacks. Since both call sites still passed `NULL` for `processed`, a successful send/recv with a legacy callback registered causes a NULL pointer dereference. The fix simply passes `msgs_processed` (the real out-parameter already available in scope) instead of `NULL` at both call sites, matching the upstream fix commit 380ff1448596926fc9d252c8e4c2720b006ef912.
